Before answering, you may run experiments on the unit, up to 3 times. To do so, reply with only {"edits": [...]} listing up to 8 edits of photos in the grid; you will see each edited photo exactly as the network sees it, with the unit's activation on the same 0-10 scale (one decimal). Each edit is {"photo": n, "op": ..., ...} where n is the grid number and op is one of:
- "occlude" with "box": [left, top, right, bottom]: grey out that box
- "keep" with "box": grey out everything outside that box
- "zoom" with "box": crop to that box and enlarge it to the full frame
- "flip": mirror left-right; "gray": remove colour
- "rotate" with "degrees"
- "shrink" with "factor" between 0.2 and 1: shrink the photo onto a grey frame
- "transform" with "name", one of: grayscale (removes all chromatic information), low_pass (removes high spatial frequencies), high_pass (removes low spatial frequencies below about 10 cycles per image), phase_scramble (removes all spatial structure carried by fourier phase), patch_shuffle_4x4 (removes global configuration), rotate_90 (removes absolute orientation), edge_map (removes colour, shading, surface reflectance, texture inside regions, edge contrast magnitude and contrast polarity), luminance_polarity_inversion (removes the sign of luminance contrast), rotate_180 (removes upright orientation), mirror (removes left-right orientation)
Boxes are fractions (0-1) of the photo as shown in the grid. When you are ready, reply with the JSON answer described below instead.
---
Task: say what this unit does. Reply with only a JSON object:
{"class": "one" | "one_plus_related" | "unrelated" | "cannot_tell",
 "explanation": "at most two sentences: what the unit responds to",
 "evidence": "at most two sentences: what in the data supports this",
 "missing_data": "what other data would most change your answer, or \"none\"",
 "confidence": a number from 0 to 1}
Class meanings: "one" = it responds to one thing; "one_plus_related" = one main thing plus weaker, related extensions; "unrelated" = two or more things with no meaningful connection; "cannot_tell" = this data is not enough to say.
